chunks: And a group informed me from Abu Muhammad Harun ibn Musa al-Tal'kabari, who said: Informed me Abu Ali Ahmad ibn Ali, known as Ibn al-Khadib al-Razi, who said: Narrated to me some of our companions from Hanzala ibn Zakariya al-Tamimi, from Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Tusi, from Abu Bakr Abdullah ibn Abi Shaibah, from Muhammad ibn Fudayl, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, who said:

Jibraeel (peace be upon him) descended with a scroll from Allah to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), in which were twelve seals of gold. He said to him: 'Surely, Allah the Exalted sends you greetings and commands you to deliver this scroll to the noble one from your family after you. He will break the first seal and act according to what is in it. When he passes away, he will deliver it to his successor after him. Thus, the first will deliver it to the last, one after another.' The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) did as he was ordered. Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) broke the first one and acted according to what was in it, then delivered it to al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who broke his seal and acted according to what was in it. He delivered it after him to al-Husayn (peace be upon him), then al-Husayn delivered it to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), and so on, one after another, until it reaches the last of them (peace be upon them all).

key_terms.الْآخِرُ: The last (referring to the final Imam)
key_terms.الْأَوَّلُ: The first (referring to the first Imam)

ai.seo_question: What is the hadith about the twelve golden seals passed down from the Prophet to the Imams?
ai.summary: This narration from Ibn Abbas, cited by Al-Tusi in *Kitab al-Ghayba*, provides a Sunni-chain (Isnad) validation for the doctrine of the Twelve Imams, framing their succession as a divine mandate delivered via a scroll with twelve golden seals. It emphasizes the sequential, hereditary nature of the Imamate, where each Imam unlocks the next stage of authority, culminating in the final Imam, thereby reinforcing the concept of *Nass* (designation) within Shia theology.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 98 - A group of scholar informed me from Abu Muhammad Harun bin Musa Talakbari that he said: Informed me Abu Ali Ahmad bin Ali, alias Ibn Qazib Razi that: Narrated to me some of our scholars from Hanzala bin Zakariya Tamimi from Ahmad bin Yahya Tusi from Abu Bakr Abdullah bin Abi Shaibah from Muhammad bin Fudail from Amash from Abu Salih from Ibn Abbas that he said:

Jibraeel (a.s) descended with a book from Allah upon the Messenger of Allah (s), having twelve golden seals. Then he said: “Surely, Allah the High greets you and orders you to hand over this book to the chosen one from your family after you. He will open the first seal and do according to what is in it. When he is about to expire, he should hand it over to his successor after him. Thus, the first will hand over to the last, one after the other.” The Holy Prophet (s) did as he was ordered. Ali Ibn Abi Talib (a.s) opened the first of them (seals) and acted as per its instructions. Then he (a.s) handed it over to Hasan (a.s), who opened his seal and acted on it. He (a.s) handed over to Husain (a.s), who passed it on to Ali Ibn Husain (a.s). This went on from one to another till it reached the last one amongst them.
